**Harrison Ford** (born July 13, 1942) is an American actor. Regarded as a cinematic cultural icon,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-1) Ford's accolades include nominations for an Academy Award, a British Academy Film Award, two Emmy Awards, five Golden Globes and two SAG-AFTRA's Actor Awards. He is also the recipient of the AFI Life Achievement Award, Cecil B. DeMille Award, Honorary César, [Honorary Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_Palme_d'Or "Honorary Palme d'Or") and SAG-AFTRA Life Achievement Award.

After making his screen debut in 1966 and early supporting roles in the films _American Graffiti_ (1973) and _The Conversation_ (1974), Ford achieved global stardom for portraying Han Solo in the space opera film _Star Wars_ (1977), a role he reprised in four subsequent films for the eponymous franchise spanning the next four decades. He also received recognition for his portrayal of the titular character in the _Indiana Jones_ franchise (1981–2023); Rick Deckard in the _Blade Runner_ franchise (1982–2017); and Jack Ryan in the action thriller films _Patriot Games_ (1992) and _Clear and Present Danger_ (1994). These roles established him as an action hero and one of Hollywood's most bankable stars from the late 1970s into the early 2000s.
Ford's performance in the thriller film _Witness_ (1985) earned him his sole Oscar nomination for Best Actor. His other films include _The Mosquito Coast_ (1986); _Working Girl_ (1988); _Presumed Innocent_ (1990); _The Fugitive_ (1993); _Sabrina_ (1995); _[The Devil's Own](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devil's\_Own "The Devil's Own")_ (1997); _Air Force One_ (1997); _Six Days, Seven Nights_ (1998); _What Lies Beneath_ (2000); _K-19: The Widowmaker_ (2002); _Cowboys & Aliens_ (2011); _42_ (2013); _The Age of Adaline_ (2015); _The Call of the Wild_ (2020); and _Captain America: Brave New World_ (2025). Ford has also starred in the Paramount+ western series _1923_ (2022–2025) and the Apple TV+ comedy series _Shrinking_ (since 2023), earning two nominations at the Primetime Emmy Awards for the latter.

Outside acting, Ford is a licensed pilot. He has often assisted the emergency services in rescue missions near his home in Wyoming and he chaired an aviation education program for youth from 2004 to 2009.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Assist-2) Ford is also an environmental activist, having served as the inaugural vice chair of Conservation International since 1991. He is married to actress Calista Flockhart.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-3)

## Early life and education
Harrison Ford was born on July 13, 1942,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199316-5) at the Swedish Covenant Hospital in the Lincoln Square community area of Chicago, Illinois,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-6) to Dorothy (née Nidelman) and advertising executive and former vaudeville and radio actor John William "Christopher" Ford.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Fordbook1-7) His mother has been described as a radio actress, but Harrison Ford denies this, and the attribution may be due to confusion with the unrelated actress and model Dorothy Ford.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-8)

## Early life and education
Ford's father was an Irish Catholic,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Fordbook1-7) his mother an Ashkenazi Jew whose parents were emigrants from Minsk.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Fordbook1-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-9) Ford described his upbringing as not so much about religious instruction, but more that he and his younger brother Terence were "raised Democrat", to be "liberals of every stripe."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-10) When asked on _Inside the Actors Studio_ about the influence of his Irish Catholic and Russian Jewish ancestry, he quipped, "As a man I've always felt Irish, as an actor I've always felt Jewish."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-tca-12) Ford was a Boy Scout, achieving the second-highest rank of Life Scout.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-13) When he was 16,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199379-14) he worked at Napowan Adventure Base Scout Camp as a counselor for the Reptile Study merit badge.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-15) He showed an affinity for snakes, collecting them for display and comparison.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199379-14) He also raised domesticated rats from a young age.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199317%E2%80%9318-16)

## Career
### 2015–present: Return to franchise roles and _Shrinking_
Ford reprised the role of Indiana Jones in _Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny_ (2023), which he later stated would be his last appearance as the character.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-94) The film received generally positive reviews, with many critics highlighting Ford's performance.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-95) In February 2025, Ford starred alongside Anthony Mackie (the new Captain America) as Thaddeus Ross in the Marvel Cinematic Universe film _Captain America: Brave New World_, replacing William Hurt after the latter's death.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-96) That same month, he brought attention to an ongoing strike by video game actors when he voiced support for Troy Baker playing the role of Indiana Jones in the video game _Indiana Jones and the Great Circle_, speaking out against the use of artificial intelligence.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-97)

## Personal life
Ford and Calista Flockhart at the 2009 Deauville American Film Festival
Ford has been married three times, has four biological children and one adopted child. He was first married to Mary Marquardt from 1964 until their divorce in 1979. They had two sons, born in 1966 and 1969. The older son once co-owned Ford's Filling Station, a gastropub located at Terminal 5 in Los Angeles International Airport.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-98) The younger son is owner of the Ludwig Clothing company[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-99) and previously owned Strong Sports Gym[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-100) and the Kim Sing Theater.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-101)
Ford's second marriage was to screenwriter Melissa Mathison from March 1983 until their separation in 2000;[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-102) they divorced in 2004.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-103) They had a son, born in 1987 and a daughter, born in 1990. Mathison died in 2015.

## Personal life
Ford began dating actress Calista Flockhart after they met at the 2002 Golden Globe Awards. He proposed to Flockhart over Valentine's Day weekend in 2009.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-104) They married on June 15, 2010, in Santa Fe, New Mexico, where Ford was filming _Cowboys & Aliens_.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-105) They are the parents of a son, born in 2001, whom Flockhart had adopted before meeting Ford. Ford and Flockhart live on an 800-acre (320-hectare; 3.2-square-kilometre) ranch in Jackson, Wyoming, where he has lived since the 1980s and approximately half of which he has donated as a nature reserve.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-106) They retain a house in the Brentwood neighborhood of Los Angeles.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-107) Ford is one of Hollywood's most private actors, guarding much of his personal life.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-tca-12) Although Ford's fans have speculated that he has social anxiety disorder, he said in 2023 that he instead has "an abhorrence of boring situations".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Hibberd-68)
In her 2016 autobiography _The Princess Diarist_, Carrie Fisher wrote that she and Ford had a three-month affair in 1976 during the filming of _Star Wars_.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-108)

## Personal life
Ford has expressed support for film director Roman Polanski, with whom he worked on the film _Frantic_. Polanski won an Oscar for directing _The Pianist_ in 2003, but has avoided setting foot on US soil due to having fled the country in the 1970s after pleading guilty to a charge of unlawful sexual intercourse with a minor.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-109) Ford brought the Oscar statuette to Paris and presented it to Polanski.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-110) In 2009, Ford signed a petition calling for Polanski's release after his arrest in Switzerland for the 1977 charge.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-111)
In his early 20s, Ford got into a car crash on a blind curve in Laguna Canyon. The crash left a scar on his chin below his lips, which was later written into his films _Working Girl_ and _Indiana Jones and_ _The Last Crusade._[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199313%E2%80%9314-113)

## Aviation
Ford touring the Air Force Museum in Dayton in 2003
Ford is a licensed pilot of both fixed-wing aircraft and helicopters.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-tca-12) On several occasions, he has provided emergency helicopter services at the request of local authorities in Wyoming. In 2000, he airlifted an EMT to a 20-year-old hiker who was suffering from dehydration on Table Mountain.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Assist-2)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-114) The following year, he was flagged down in his helicopter by a 13-year-old Boy Scout who got lost near Yellowstone National Park.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-115)
Ford began flight training in the 1960s at Wild Rose Idlewild Airport in Wild Rose, Wisconsin, flying in a Piper PA-22 Tri-Pacer, but at $15 an hour (equivalent to $160 in 2025), he could not afford to continue the training.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-116) In the mid-1990s, he bought a used Gulfstream II and asked one of his pilots, Terry Bender, to give him flying lessons. They started flying a Cessna 182 Skylane out of Jackson, Wyoming, later switching to Teterboro Airport in Teterboro, New Jersey, flying a Cessna 206 in which he made his first solo flight.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-117)

## Aviation
Ford's aircraft are kept at Santa Monica Airport.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-118) His Bell 407 helicopter is often hangered at Jackson and has been used by Ford in two mountain rescues during his assigned duty time with Teton County Search and Rescue. During one of the rescues, Ford recovered a lost and disoriented hiker. She boarded his helicopter and promptly vomited into one of the rescuers' caps, unaware of who the pilot was until much later; "I can't believe I barfed in Harrison Ford's helicopter!" she said later.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-119)
Ford flies his de Havilland Canada DHC-2 Beaver (registration N28S) more than any of his other aircraft and has repeatedly said that he likes this aircraft and the sound of its Pratt & Whitney R-985 radial engine.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-120) According to Ford, it had been flown in the CIA's Air America operations and was riddled with bullet holes that had to be patched up.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-121)
Ford's 2010 International Air & Space Hall of Fame portrait in the Air & Space Museum in San Diego

## Aviation
In March 2004, Ford became chairman of the Experimental Aircraft Association (EAA)'s Young Eagles program, founded by then-EAA president Tom Poberezny and fellow actor-pilot Cliff Robertson. Ford was asked to take the position by Greg Anderson, Senior Vice President of the EAA at the time, to replace General Chuck Yeager, who was vacating the post that he had held for many years. Ford at first was hesitant, but later accepted the offer and has made appearances with the Young Eagles at the EAA AirVenture Oshkosh gathering at Oshkosh, Wisconsin, for two years. In July 2005, at the gathering in Oshkosh, Ford agreed to accept the position for another two years. He has flown over 280 children as part of the Young Eagles program, usually in his DHC-2 Beaver, which can seat the actor and five children. Ford stepped down as program chairman in 2009 and was replaced by Captain Chesley Sullenberger and First Officer Jeff Skiles. He is involved with the EAA chapter in Driggs, Idaho, just over the Teton Range from Jackson, Wyoming. On July 28, 2016, Ford flew the two millionth Young Eagle at the EAA AirVenture convention,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-122) making it the most successful youth aviation introduction program in history.
As of 2009, Ford appears in Internet advertisements for General Aviation Serves America, a campaign by the advocacy group Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA).[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-123) He has also appeared in several independent aviation documentaries, including _Wings Over the Rockies_ (2009),[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-124)_Flying the Feathered Edge: The Bob Hoover Project_ (2014) and _Living in the Age of Airplanes_ (2015).[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-125)

## Aviation
Ford is an honorary board member of the humanitarian aviation organization Wings of Hope,[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-126) and has made several trips to Washington, D.C., to fight for pilots' rights.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Flyingmag51Heroes-127) He has also donated substantial funds to aerobatic champion Sean Tucker's charitable program, The Bob Hoover Academy (named after legendary aviator Bob Hoover), which educates at-risk teens in central California and teaches them how to fly.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-128)

## Aviation
### Incidents
On August 22, 1987, Ford was traveling as a passenger with Clint Eastwood and Sondra Locke aboard a Gulfstream III when the jet developed an engine fire and stuck landing gear during a Paris-to-L.A. flight and was forced to land in Bangor, Maine.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-129) The charter company owning the G-3 sent another jet and mechanics to Bangor and the group flew out on that plane the next day.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-130)
On October 23, 1999, Ford was involved in the crash of a Bell 206L4 LongRanger helicopter. The NTSB accident report states that Ford was piloting the aircraft over the Lake Piru riverbed near Santa Clarita, California, on a routine training flight. While making his second attempt at an autorotation with powered recovery,[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-131) the aircraft was unable to recover power after the sudden drop in altitude. It landed hard and skidded forward in the loose gravel before flipping onto its side. Neither Ford nor the instructor pilot suffered any injuries, though the helicopter was seriously damaged.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-132)
On March 5, 2015, Ford's plane, believed to be a Ryan PT-22 Recruit, made an emergency landing on the Penmar Golf Course in Venice, California, after it lost engine power. He was taken to Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center, where he was reported to be in fair to moderate condition.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-133) Ford suffered a broken pelvis and broken ankle during the accident, as well as other injuries.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-134)

## Early life and education
Harrison Ford was born on July 13, 1942,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199316-5) at the Swedish Covenant Hospital in the Lincoln Square community area of Chicago, Illinois,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-6) to Dorothy (née Nidelman) and advertising executive and former vaudeville and radio actor John William "Christopher" Ford.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Fordbook1-7) His mother has been described as a radio actress, but Harrison Ford denies this, and the attribution may be due to confusion with the unrelated actress and model Dorothy Ford.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-8)
texts.4:
## Early life and education
Ford's father was an Irish Catholic,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Fordbook1-7) his mother an Ashkenazi Jew whose parents were emigrants from Minsk.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Fordbook1-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-9) Ford described his upbringing as not so much about religious instruction, but more that he and his younger brother Terence were "raised Democrat", to be "liberals of every stripe."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-10) When asked on _Inside the Actors Studio_ about the influence of his Irish Catholic and Russian Jewish ancestry, he quipped, "As a man I've always felt Irish, as an actor I've always felt Jewish."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-tca-12) Ford was a Boy Scout, achieving the second-highest rank of Life Scout.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-13) When he was 16,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199379-14) he worked at Napowan Adventure Base Scout Camp as a counselor for the Reptile Study merit badge.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-15) He showed an affinity for snakes, collecting them for display and comparison.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199379-14) He also raised domesticated rats from a young age.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199317%E2%80%9318-16)

## Career
### 2015–present: Return to franchise roles and _Shrinking_
Ford reprised the role of Indiana Jones in _Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny_ (2023), which he later stated would be his last appearance as the character.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-94) The film received generally positive reviews, with many critics highlighting Ford's performance.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-95) In February 2025, Ford starred alongside Anthony Mackie (the new Captain America) as Thaddeus Ross in the Marvel Cinematic Universe film _Captain America: Brave New World_, replacing William Hurt after the latter's death.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-96) That same month, he brought attention to an ongoing strike by video game actors when he voiced support for Troy Baker playing the role of Indiana Jones in the video game _Indiana Jones and the Great Circle_, speaking out against the use of artificial intelligence.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-97)

## Personal life
Ford and Calista Flockhart at the 2009 Deauville American Film Festival
Ford has been married three times, has four biological children and one adopted child. He was first married to Mary Marquardt from 1964 until their divorce in 1979. They had two sons, born in 1966 and 1969. The older son once co-owned Ford's Filling Station, a gastropub located at Terminal 5 in Los Angeles International Airport.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-98) The younger son is owner of the Ludwig Clothing company[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-99) and previously owned Strong Sports Gym[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-100) and the Kim Sing Theater.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-101)
Ford's second marriage was to screenwriter Melissa Mathison from March 1983 until their separation in 2000;[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-102) they divorced in 2004.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-103) They had a son, born in 1987 and a daughter, born in 1990. Mathison died in 2015.
texts.27:
## Personal life
Ford began dating actress Calista Flockhart after they met at the 2002 Golden Globe Awards. He proposed to Flockhart over Valentine's Day weekend in 2009.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-104) They married on June 15, 2010, in Santa Fe, New Mexico, where Ford was filming _Cowboys & Aliens_.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-105) They are the parents of a son, born in 2001, whom Flockhart had adopted before meeting Ford. Ford and Flockhart live on an 800-acre (320-hectare; 3.2-square-kilometre) ranch in Jackson, Wyoming, where he has lived since the 1980s and approximately half of which he has donated as a nature reserve.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-106) They retain a house in the Brentwood neighborhood of Los Angeles.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-107) Ford is one of Hollywood's most private actors, guarding much of his personal life.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-tca-12) Although Ford's fans have speculated that he has social anxiety disorder, he said in 2023 that he instead has "an abhorrence of boring situations".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Hibberd-68)
In her 2016 autobiography _The Princess Diarist_, Carrie Fisher wrote that she and Ford had a three-month affair in 1976 during the filming of _Star Wars_.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-108)

## Personal life
Ford has expressed support for film director Roman Polanski, with whom he worked on the film _Frantic_. Polanski won an Oscar for directing _The Pianist_ in 2003, but has avoided setting foot on US soil due to having fled the country in the 1970s after pleading guilty to a charge of unlawful sexual intercourse with a minor.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-109) Ford brought the Oscar statuette to Paris and presented it to Polanski.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-110) In 2009, Ford signed a petition calling for Polanski's release after his arrest in Switzerland for the 1977 charge.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-111)
In his early 20s, Ford got into a car crash on a blind curve in Laguna Canyon. The crash left a scar on his chin below his lips, which was later written into his films _Working Girl_ and _Indiana Jones and_ _The Last Crusade._[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199313%E2%80%9314-113)

## Aviation
Ford touring the Air Force Museum in Dayton in 2003
Ford is a licensed pilot of both fixed-wing aircraft and helicopters.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-tca-12) On several occasions, he has provided emergency helicopter services at the request of local authorities in Wyoming. In 2000, he airlifted an EMT to a 20-year-old hiker who was suffering from dehydration on Table Mountain.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Assist-2)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-114) The following year, he was flagged down in his helicopter by a 13-year-old Boy Scout who got lost near Yellowstone National Park.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-115)
Ford began flight training in the 1960s at Wild Rose Idlewild Airport in Wild Rose, Wisconsin, flying in a Piper PA-22 Tri-Pacer, but at $15 an hour (equivalent to $160 in 2025), he could not afford to continue the training.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-116) In the mid-1990s, he bought a used Gulfstream II and asked one of his pilots, Terry Bender, to give him flying lessons. They started flying a Cessna 182 Skylane out of Jackson, Wyoming, later switching to Teterboro Airport in Teterboro, New Jersey, flying a Cessna 206 in which he made his first solo flight.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-117)

## Aviation
Ford's aircraft are kept at Santa Monica Airport.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-118) His Bell 407 helicopter is often hangered at Jackson and has been used by Ford in two mountain rescues during his assigned duty time with Teton County Search and Rescue. During one of the rescues, Ford recovered a lost and disoriented hiker. She boarded his helicopter and promptly vomited into one of the rescuers' caps, unaware of who the pilot was until much later; "I can't believe I barfed in Harrison Ford's helicopter!" she said later.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-119)
Ford flies his de Havilland Canada DHC-2 Beaver (registration N28S) more than any of his other aircraft and has repeatedly said that he likes this aircraft and the sound of its Pratt & Whitney R-985 radial engine.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-120) According to Ford, it had been flown in the CIA's Air America operations and was riddled with bullet holes that had to be patched up.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-121)

## Aviation
In March 2004, Ford became chairman of the Experimental Aircraft Association (EAA)'s Young Eagles program, founded by then-EAA president Tom Poberezny and fellow actor-pilot Cliff Robertson. Ford was asked to take the position by Greg Anderson, Senior Vice President of the EAA at the time, to replace General Chuck Yeager, who was vacating the post that he had held for many years. Ford at first was hesitant, but later accepted the offer and has made appearances with the Young Eagles at the EAA AirVenture Oshkosh gathering at Oshkosh, Wisconsin, for two years. In July 2005, at the gathering in Oshkosh, Ford agreed to accept the position for another two years. He has flown over 280 children as part of the Young Eagles program, usually in his DHC-2 Beaver, which can seat the actor and five children. Ford stepped down as program chairman in 2009 and was replaced by Captain Chesley Sullenberger and First Officer Jeff Skiles. He is involved with the EAA chapter in Driggs, Idaho, just over the Teton Range from Jackson, Wyoming. On July 28, 2016, Ford flew the two millionth Young Eagle at the EAA AirVenture convention,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-122) making it the most successful youth aviation introduction program in history.
As of 2009, Ford appears in Internet advertisements for General Aviation Serves America, a campaign by the advocacy group Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA).[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-123) He has also appeared in several independent aviation documentaries, including _Wings Over the Rockies_ (2009),[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-124)_Flying the Feathered Edge: The Bob Hoover Project_ (2014) and _Living in the Age of Airplanes_ (2015).[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-125)
texts.32:
## Aviation
Ford is an honorary board member of the humanitarian aviation organization Wings of Hope,[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-126) and has made several trips to Washington, D.C., to fight for pilots' rights.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Flyingmag51Heroes-127) He has also donated substantial funds to aerobatic champion Sean Tucker's charitable program, The Bob Hoover Academy (named after legendary aviator Bob Hoover), which educates at-risk teens in central California and teaches them how to fly.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-128)
texts.33:
## Aviation
### Incidents
On August 22, 1987, Ford was traveling as a passenger with Clint Eastwood and Sondra Locke aboard a Gulfstream III when the jet developed an engine fire and stuck landing gear during a Paris-to-L.A. flight and was forced to land in Bangor, Maine.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-129) The charter company owning the G-3 sent another jet and mechanics to Bangor and the group flew out on that plane the next day.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-130)
On October 23, 1999, Ford was involved in the crash of a Bell 206L4 LongRanger helicopter. The NTSB accident report states that Ford was piloting the aircraft over the Lake Piru riverbed near Santa Clarita, California, on a routine training flight. While making his second attempt at an autorotation with powered recovery,[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-131) the aircraft was unable to recover power after the sudden drop in altitude. It landed hard and skidded forward in the loose gravel before flipping onto its side. Neither Ford nor the instructor pilot suffered any injuries, though the helicopter was seriously damaged.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-132)
On March 5, 2015, Ford's plane, believed to be a Ryan PT-22 Recruit, made an emergency landing on the Penmar Golf Course in Venice, California, after it lost engine power. He was taken to Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center, where he was reported to be in fair to moderate condition.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-133) Ford suffered a broken pelvis and broken ankle during the accident, as well as other injuries.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-134)

Ford's father was an Irish Catholic,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Fordbook1-7) his mother an Ashkenazi Jew whose parents were emigrants from Minsk.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Fordbook1-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-9) Ford described his upbringing as not so much about religious instruction, but more that he and his younger brother Terence were "raised Democrat", to be "liberals of every stripe."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-10) When asked on _Inside the Actors Studio_ about the influence of his Irish Catholic and Russian Jewish ancestry, he quipped, "As a man I've always felt Irish, as an actor I've always felt Jewish."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-tca-12) Ford was a Boy Scout, achieving the second-highest rank of Life Scout.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-13) When he was 16,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199379-14) he worked at Napowan Adventure Base Scout Camp as a counselor for the Reptile Study merit badge.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-15) He showed an affinity for snakes, collecting them for display and comparison.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199379-14) He also raised domesticated rats from a young age.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-FOOTNOTESellers199317%E2%80%9318-16)

## Aviation
In March 2004, Ford became chairman of the Experimental Aircraft Association (EAA)'s Young Eagles program, founded by then-EAA president Tom Poberezny and fellow actor-pilot Cliff Robertson. Ford was asked to take the position by Greg Anderson, Senior Vice President of the EAA at the time, to replace General Chuck Yeager, who was vacating the post that he had held for many years. Ford at first was hesitant, but later accepted the offer and has made appearances with the Young Eagles at the EAA AirVenture Oshkosh gathering at Oshkosh, Wisconsin, for two years. In July 2005, at the gathering in Oshkosh, Ford agreed to accept the position for another two years. He has flown over 280 children as part of the Young Eagles program, usually in his DHC-2 Beaver, which can seat the actor and five children. Ford stepped down as program chairman in 2009 and was replaced by Captain Chesley Sullenberger and First Officer Jeff Skiles. He is involved with the EAA chapter in Driggs, Idaho, just over the Teton Range from Jackson, Wyoming. On July 28, 2016, Ford flew the two millionth Young Eagle at the EAA AirVenture convention,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-122) making it the most successful youth aviation introduction program in history.
As of 2009, Ford appears in Internet advertisements for General Aviation Serves America, a campaign by the advocacy group Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA).[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-123) He has also appeared in several independent aviation documentaries, including _Wings Over the Rockies_ (2009),[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-124)_Flying the Feathered Edge: The Bob Hoover Project_ (2014) and _Living in the Age of Airplanes_ (2015).[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-125)

Ford is an honorary board member of the humanitarian aviation organization Wings of Hope,[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-126) and has made several trips to Washington, D.C., to fight for pilots' rights.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-Flyingmag51Heroes-127) He has also donated substantial funds to aerobatic champion Sean Tucker's charitable program, The Bob Hoover Academy (named after legendary aviator Bob Hoover), which educates at-risk teens in central California and teaches them how to fly.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-128)

On August 22, 1987, Ford was traveling as a passenger with Clint Eastwood and Sondra Locke aboard a Gulfstream III when the jet developed an engine fire and stuck landing gear during a Paris-to-L.A. flight and was forced to land in Bangor, Maine.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-129) The charter company owning the G-3 sent another jet and mechanics to Bangor and the group flew out on that plane the next day.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-130)

The NTSB accident report states that Ford was piloting the aircraft over the Lake Piru riverbed near Santa Clarita, California, on a routine training flight. While making his second attempt at an autorotation with powered recovery,[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford#cite_note-131) the aircraft was unable to recover power after the sudden drop in altitude.
